item.title: Evooo1Bot Mirai-Based Linux Botnet Turns Routers Into SOCKS5 Relay Nodes
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Aug 14:00 → 15 Aug 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

New Evooo1Bot Linux botnet turns routers into traffic relay nodes — Should Read

A new Mirai-based Linux botnet called Evooo1Bot is exploiting known flaws in internet-facing routers and gateway devices to turn them into SOCKS5 proxy relays, steal credentials, brute-force SSH, and launch DDoS attacks. Defenders should patch IoT firmware, change default credentials, disable remote admin access, and replace unsupported devices.

  • A new Mirai-based modular Linux botnet malware called Evooo1Bot is targeting internet-facing gateway devices and turning them into SOCKS5 traffic relay nodes.
  • Evooo1Bot has been targeting devices from Alcatel, NETGEAR, Tenda, Mitsubishi Electric, Telesquare, and D-Link since at least July by exploiting known vulnerabilities.
  • Fortinet researchers said Evooo1Bot extends Mirai with encrypted command-and-control communications, an SSH brute-force scanner, a SOCKS relay module, a credential sniffer, and an integrated exploit arsenal.
  • Newer Evooo1Bot builds include a separate vulnerability-exploitation module targeting Hikvision cameras, Atlassian Confluence, Zyxel firewalls, TP-Link routers, D-Link NAS devices, WSO2 products, Kubernetes ingress-nginx, and vulnerable PHP-CGI installations.
  • The malware establishes persistence through systemd, SysV init, shell profiles, and rc.local, while a cron job attempts to re-download the payload every five minutes.

Technologies: router, proxy, firewall, nas, orchestration, container-platform, operating-system, iot-device

Products: evooo1bot, mirai, confluence, ingress-nginx, php-cgi, systemd, sysv-init

Vendors: fortinet, alcatel, netgear, tenda, mitsubishi-electric, telesquare, d-link, hikvision, atlassian, zyxel, tp-link, wso2, kubernetes, php

item.title: Hijacked Nonprofit Mailbox Abuses Real Grant Thread via Dynamics 365 Redirect
item.content:encoded:
Window: 15 Aug 10:00 → 15 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

The Grant Thread Was Real. The Portal Was Not. — Should Read

Attackers abused a compromised nonprofit Google Workspace mailbox to resend a genuine federal grant thread to unrelated recipients, adding only a phishing link disguised as grant documents. The lure bypassed basic trust checks by using real correspondence and a Microsoft Dynamics 365 marketing redirect, making behavioral signals like first-time sender, Bcc delivery, and recipient mismatch the key detections.

  • A compromised nonprofit Google Workspace mailbox reused a genuine federal grant notification containing real grant metadata and hotlinked GrantSolutions images as the credibility layer for a phishing message.
  • The message was blind-copied to an operations executive at a professional services firm who had no relationship to the grant or the original nonprofit recipients.
  • The only new call to action pointed to a Microsoft Dynamics 365 marketing redirect URL that the static link scanner rated clean.
  • A live screenshot of the linked page showed PNC Foundation grant opportunity branding and access gated behind a work or business email field, but no testing was performed beyond that page.
  • Themis scored the message at 82% confidence for credential theft and the incident was automatically resolved as phishing for the single affected mailbox.

Technologies: email-security

Products: dynamics-365, google-workspace, themis, grantsolutions

Vendors: microsoft, google, ironscales, grantsolutions

item.title: Taiwan Agentic AI Breach and Anthropic Claude Text Watermarking
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Aug 22:00 → 15 Aug 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

The Agentic AI threat cluster: Seven incidents, three actors, and what they mean for your exposure — Must Read

Tenable says a seven-incident cluster shows near-autonomous AI cyber operations are now operational, with the Taiwan government attack demonstrating agents can rapidly map systems, compromise accounts, and exfiltrate data by abusing exposed identity infrastructure and weak authentication. The key defensive takeaway is to reduce discoverable authentication surfaces, harden SSO and credentials, and add behavioral detection for machine-speed reconnaissance and credential attacks.

  • Taiwan’s Ministry of Digital Affairs confirmed that a near-autonomous AI cyber attack in July 2026 mapped 21 connected government systems, compromised 85 accounts, and exfiltrated more than 2,564 personnel records in approximately four days.
  • Tenable’s Research Special Operations team is tracking the Taiwan campaign as part of a seven-incident agentic AI threat cluster spanning November 2025 through August 2026.
  • The Taiwan operators used a multi-agent framework assembled from Hermes Agent and OpenClaw, and the agents scraped public authentication metadata, followed a JavaScript-linked GitBook SSO guide, and pulled exploitation techniques from public vulnerability databases and GitHub in real time.
  • Tenable states that the common entry point across the cluster is identity and authentication exposure, including discoverable federation endpoints, weak credentials, and misconfigured single sign-on.
  • The article says the broader cluster includes JADEPUFFER’s exploitation of CVE-2025-3248 in Langflow for automated database extortion and knaithe/KnYuan’s use of Hermes Agent with DeepSeek for autonomous vulnerability scanning.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, vpn, load-balancer, web-server, firewall

Products: tenable-one, tenable-one-attack-surface-management, tenable-one-identity-exposure, tenable-one-vulnerability-management, tenable-one-web-app-scanning, hermes-agent, openclaw, deepseek, langflow, n8n, citrix-netscaler, marimo-notebook, apache-tomcat, pan-os, windows-ike-vpn, keycloak, gitbook

Vendors: tenable, langflow, n8n, citrix, marimo, apache, palo-alto-networks, microsoft, keycloak, gitbook, deepseek, hermes-agent, openclaw

How Anthropic plans to watermark Claude's AI-generated text — May Read

Anthropic will add invisible text watermarking to Claude outputs worldwide to comply with the EU AI Act, using statistical patterns in token choices rather than hidden characters. The watermark can be checked through a planned detection API, but it works best on longer, more creative text and may be weaker for code, factual answers, or heavily rewritten content.

  • Anthropic plans to add invisible watermarking to future Claude-generated text worldwide as part of its compliance with the EU AI Act and the EU Code of Practice.
  • Anthropic says Claude’s text watermark does not add visible markers, hidden characters, extra tokens, added cost, or a practical impact on creativity, readability, content quality, or generation speed.
  • The watermarking approach is based on Google DeepMind’s SynthID-Text and works by using a secret key to influence some of Claude’s random word choices during generation, creating a statistical pattern detectable by someone with the key.
  • Anthropic says watermarking is weaker or not applied when an exact output is required, such as factual answers or code, and detection is less reliable for short text or light proofreading of human-written text.
  • Anthropic plans to offer a watermark detection API that can estimate whether Claude was likely involved in writing text, while generated PNG, JPG, and SVG files will use cryptographically signed C2PA provenance metadata instead of text-style watermarking.

Products: claude, synthid-text

Vendors: anthropic, google-deepmind

item.title: Germany and Brazil Arrest Suspects in €30M Commerzbank Service Provider Fraud
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Aug 18:00 → 14 Aug 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers arrested over €30M bank fraud exploiting service provider flaw — Should Read

Brazilian and European authorities arrested or charged suspects accused of exploiting a service-provider software flaw to trigger unauthorized direct debits from Commerzbank customer accounts, causing about €30 million in losses. Commerzbank said affected customers did not suffer financial losses.

  • Four cybercriminals were arrested in Brazil and three others were charged in Europe over allegations that they exploited a vulnerability at a service provider to withdraw funds from Commerzbank customers’ bank accounts.
  • The theft occurred over four days in November 2023 and caused losses of around €30 million, according to the investigation by Brazilian and German federal police agencies.
  • Commerzbank confirmed that its clients were impacted by unauthorized direct debits caused by technical issues at a service provider, but said customers suffered no financial loss.
  • German authorities said the attackers exploited a software vulnerability introduced by a faulty software update at the payment and transaction-processing system of a financial institution.
  • Investigators said the stolen funds were moved and concealed through pass-through accounts, companies, payment institutions, virtual-asset platforms, and payment cards issued without the beneficiaries’ consent.

item.title: CVE-2026-65400 macOS Exploitation, Qilin Ransomware, and Google Workspace OAuth Risks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Aug 14:00 → 14 Aug 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers exploit macOS Screen Sharing flaw to deploy Monero miner — Must Read

Hackers are actively exploiting a macOS Screen Sharing authentication bypass flaw, CVE-2026-65400, on internet-exposed systems to gain root access and install a Monero miner. Users should install Apple’s latest macOS updates or disable Screen Sharing if it is not needed.

  • The Netherlands’ National Cyber Security Centre warned that hackers are actively exploiting a macOS Screen Sharing authentication bypass vulnerability after public exploit code emerged.
  • Apple fixed CVE-2026-65400 on August 6 in macOS Tahoe 26.6.1 and earlier releases, with updates also available for macOS Sequoia 15.7.9 and macOS Sonoma 14.8.9.
  • The flaw allows network-based attackers to gain access without valid credentials when macOS Screen Sharing is exposed over TCP port 5900.
  • The NCSC said it received reports of active exploitation on multiple systems where port 5900 was accessible from the internet.
  • According to the NCSC, attackers obtained root access on affected systems and placed a Monero cryptocurrency miner.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access

Products: macos-screen-sharing, macos-tahoe, macos-sequoia, macos-sonoma

Vendors: apple

Ransomware Threats in the Americas H1 2026: Dissecting the Regional Attack Patterns and Dominant Actors — Should Read

The Americas accounted for 57% of all ransomware incidents tracked globally in H1 2026, with the U.S. as the main target and Qilin the top regional actor. North America faces a crowded RaaS ecosystem, while South America is more concentrated around The Gentlemen, requiring different defensive priorities by region and sector.

  • Cyble Research and Intelligence Labs tracked 2,188 documented ransomware attacks in North and South America between January and June 2026, representing more than 57% of the 3,836 ransomware incidents tracked worldwide.
  • North America recorded 1,981 ransomware attacks in H1 2026, while South America recorded 207 attacks, with the article describing North America as a saturated market and South America as more concentrated around fewer operators.
  • Qilin was the most active ransomware group across the Americas with 410 documented incidents, while The Gentlemen was the most active group specifically in South America with 46 incidents.
  • The United States accounted for 1,721 ransomware attacks, representing 78.7% of Americas ransomware activity and nearly 45% of global ransomware volume tracked in the article.
  • The article identifies Professional Services, Manufacturing, Construction, Healthcare, BFSI, Agriculture and Livestock, and Government and Law Enforcement as sectors facing notable ransomware or related cyber threats across the Americas.

The Modern Attack Chain: Rethinking Google Workspace Security in the Age of AI — Optional

The article argues that Google Workspace attacks are shifting from email-led account takeovers to OAuth-token abuse that can expose Gmail, Drive, and connected apps, and that overpermissioned AI agents can create similar risks even without a malicious attacker. The key takeaway is that defenses must cover the full workspace chain—email, OAuth activity, sensitive data, and lateral movement—not just the inbox.

  • The article says the Vercel and Composio breaches followed a similar pattern in which email was not the entry point into the workspace.
  • The article describes an evolving attack chain where a stolen OAuth token provides access to Gmail and Drive, enables email account takeover, and supports lateral movement through credentials, password resets, or magic links.
  • The article warns that AI agents connected to Google Workspace use legitimate OAuth grants to read email and Drive, and can follow the same path as attackers if they behave unexpectedly or have broader access than needed.
  • The article argues that defenses should cover the full workspace chain across email, OAuth, Drive, and account behavior rather than stopping at inbox security.
  • Material Security says its platform maps to this chain by blocking email payloads, detecting suspicious OAuth behavior, finding sensitive data in email and Drive, and redacting password reset links behind step-up verification.

Technologies: cloud-platform, email-security, iam, dlp

Products: google-workspace, gmail, google-drive, material-email-security, material-oauth-agent, material-file-security

Vendors: material-security, google

Top unified security tools in 2026 — Optional

The article argues that Aikido Security is the strongest unified security platform for 2026 because it combines code, cloud, runtime, and endpoint coverage in one product with cross-layer prioritization and remediation workflows. It positions cloud-first tools like Wiz, Orca, and Cortex Cloud and AppSec tools like Snyk and Checkmarx as less complete due to weaker integration across the full SDLC.

  • The article says unified security in 2026 means one platform covering the software development lifecycle from supply chain and source code through containers, pipelines, cloud, runtime, and endpoints.
  • Aikido's State of AI in Security and Development report found that 90% of organizations using 6-8 security tools experienced an incident, compared with 64% of organizations using 1-2 tools.
  • The article ranks Aikido Security as the strongest unified security tool because it covers code, cloud, and runtime in one platform and links findings across those layers.
  • The article says Wiz, Palo Alto Cortex Cloud, and Orca Security are strong on cloud posture but treat code security as an add-on.
  • The article says Snyk is mature for code and dependencies but has no native cloud offering, while Checkmarx One has broad AppSec coverage but is weighed down by slow scans, false positives, and cost.

item.title: SAP CVE-2026-58231 Exploitation, Clop PTC Attacks, JFrog Artifactory Flaws, Major Breaches
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Aug 10:00 → 14 Aug 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Shell investigates 'potential incident' after Clop data theft claims — Must Read

Shell is investigating a possible security incident after the Clop ransomware gang claimed it stole 89GB of data, likely through attacks exploiting CVE-2026-12569 in Internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM systems. The same Clop campaign has reportedly targeted dozens of organizations, including GE and Philips.

  • Shell confirmed it is investigating a potential security incident after the Clop ransomware gang claimed it stole 89GB of data from the company.
  • Clop claimed the stolen Shell files include engineering drawings, facility testing report scans, facility photos, and project plans.
  • Shell was listed by Clop as one of 43 new victims likely targeted through Internet-exposed PTC Windchill and FlexPLM instances affected by CVE-2026-12569.
  • Clop also claimed it stole sensitive data from General Electric and Philips, including backups, system files, projects, drawings, diagrams, and blueprints.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-12569 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and ordered U.S. federal agencies to secure affected PTC Windchill and FlexPLM instances within three days.

Products: ptc-windchill, ptc-flexplm

Vendors: ptc

Max severity SAP Commerce Cloud flaw now targeted in attacks — Must Read

Attackers are already targeting CVE-2026-58231, a maximum-severity unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in SAP Commerce Cloud, just three days after SAP patched it. Organizations running exposed SAP Commerce Cloud instances should apply the update immediately and check for signs of exploitation.

  • Defused reported that CVE-2026-58231, a maximum-severity SAP Commerce Cloud remote code execution vulnerability patched three days earlier, is already being targeted in attacks.
  • CVE-2026-58231 is an improper authorization flaw in the core Data Hub Adapter extension for SAP Commerce Cloud that unauthenticated attackers can exploit in low-complexity attacks to execute arbitrary code.
  • SAP said successful exploitation of CVE-2026-58231 could compromise internal components and have a high impact on the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the application.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 4,200 IP addresses with a SAP Commerce Cloud fingerprint, mostly in Europe and North America, but the article says it is unclear how many are honeypots or already secured.
  • SAP has not yet flagged CVE-2026-58231 as actively exploited in its security advisory, while Defused said exploitation attempts are hitting its honeypots despite no public proof-of-concept being available.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: sap-commerce-cloud, data-hub-adapter, sap-hybris

Vendors: sap, defused, shadowserver

RingCentral data breach exposed info of 1.6 million accounts — Must Read

ShinyHunters stole and leaked data tied to 1.6 million RingCentral accounts after a July breach reportedly involving social engineering. Exposed records include names, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses.

  • Have I Been Pwned said leaked RingCentral data contained records for 1.6 million accounts, including names, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses.
  • RingCentral disclosed on July 28 that its systems were compromised following what it described as a sophisticated social engineering campaign.
  • RingCentral said the incident affected data for a limited portion of customers, that it is communicating with affected customers directly, and that its core platform and services were not disrupted.
  • ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for the breach on July 27 and said it had stolen 623GB of data.
  • After RingCentral refused to pay a ransom to have the stolen data destroyed, ShinyHunters leaked a compressed archive containing 280GB of files on its dark web leak site.

Products: ringcentral

Vendors: ringcentral, have-i-been-pwned

Stealing the Artifact – JFrog Artifactory Vulnerability — Should Read

NetSPI found a chain of JFrog Artifactory vulnerabilities that let an unauthenticated attacker mint an anonymous JWT, bypass authorization, and retrieve restricted artifacts from affected repositories. JFrog has patched the issues in Artifactory 7.146.8 and several supported maintenance releases.

  • NetSPI discovered vulnerabilities in JFrog Artifactory that allowed an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and authorization to retrieve an arbitrary artifact from an Artifactory repository.
  • At the time of discovery, all versions of Artifactory OSS and Artifactory Enterprise were affected by the vulnerabilities.
  • CVE-2026-42018 allowed authentication bypass to the anonymous user and was remediated in Artifactory 7.146.8.
  • CVE-2026-69107 covered potential unauthorized artifact access and was remediated in Artifactory versions 7.146.8, 7.133.21, 7.125.14, 7.117.21, 7.111.14, and 7.104.16.
  • The attack chain combined four bugs: an anonymous JWT mint authentication bypass, missing authorization in stash results, path traversal in stash export, and URL path confusion.

Technologies: package-registry, ci-cd, iam, web-server, router, load-balancer

Products: artifactory, artifactory-oss, artifactory-enterprise, aws-iam, apache-tomcat, traefik, spring-security, jf-router

Vendors: jfrog, amazon-web-services, apache-software-foundation, traefik-labs, spring

France investigates tax authority breach after hacker claims 600,000 victims — Should Read

France’s tax authority confirmed hackers accessed and extracted data from its systems after a hacker claimed to have stolen information on more than 600,000 people. Officials are investigating what was exposed and will notify affected individuals and regulators.

  • France’s Economy Ministry said an attacker gained unauthorized access to the Directorate General of Public Finances systems in late June after stealing or misusing someone’s identity.
  • The intrusion allowed the attacker to view and extract data belonging to individuals and businesses, and officials are still determining what information was accessed or stolen and how many people and businesses were affected.
  • The DGFiP said affected people will be contacted individually and told what information may have been exposed and what precautions they should take.
  • FrenchBreaches reported that a hacker using the alias ZeroBytes claimed to have obtained data on more than 600,000 people, including names, tax identification numbers, email addresses, family circumstances and tax status details.
  • The DGFiP has not publicly attributed the breach to a specific threat actor or confirmed the hacker’s claims.

The Tracking Parameter That Named the Wrong Company — May Read

A Microsoft Teams-themed phishing email used multiple nested security-vendor redirects and obfuscation to hide a likely credential-harvesting path, but a stale tracking parameter exposed reuse of the same phishing kit from a prior campaign. The key lesson is to hunt the reusable template artifacts and redirect structure rather than relying on sender authentication or recognizable vendor link wrappers.

  • A fabricated Microsoft Teams audio-message notification reached a director-level mailbox at a mid-size forensic engineering and investigative consulting firm in late July 2026.
  • The message’s button hid a four-layer redirect chain involving multiple vendor link wrappers and ultimately pointed to a payment-themed path on a Brazilian law firm’s long-registered domain.
  • A stale recipient-tracking parameter in the final redirect named an employee at an unrelated organization, indicating reused phishing-kit scaffolding rather than involvement by that organization.
  • The lure used hidden CSS, zero-width text, and injected hex-like fragments inside Microsoft Teams brand wording to make the message appear normal to humans while disrupting raw-text scanning.
  • SPF and composite authentication passed, while DKIM was absent and DMARC returned a best-guess pass, showing that authentication results did not prevent the message from being classified as credential theft.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis, adaptive-ai, microsoft-teams

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft

item.title: Citrix NetScaler Pre-Auth RCE and HoneyMyte CoolClient Rootkit Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Aug 06:00 → 14 Aug 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

APT group HoneyMyte upgrades CoolClient: the backdoor gets a kernel-level Windows rootkit — Must Read

HoneyMyte’s CoolClient backdoor has evolved to deploy a signed Windows kernel-mode rootkit that hides and protects its processes, files, registry entries, and some network activity. The updated variant was seen in PlugX-led intrusions against organizations in Asia and Russia, including government targets.

  • Kaspersky analyzed a new CoolClient variant attributed to HoneyMyte, also known as Mustang Panda, that can deploy a signed Windows kernel-mode driver as a service and communicate with it through IOCTL requests.
  • The driver, named msagent.sys, enhances stealth by hiding and protecting the CoolClient process, related files, registry entries, and selected network information such as configured C2 IPv4 addresses.
  • In observed intrusions, HoneyMyte used PlugX as the initial post-compromise implant before deploying CoolClient components through DLL sideloading with a legitimate Sangfor executable renamed as defender.exe.
  • The updated CoolClient execution chain includes libngs.dll as a first-stage loader, loadcert.ini as a second-stage component responsible for setup, injection, driver deployment, and persistence, and cert.ini as the final-stage implant for C2 communication and backdoor functionality.
  • Researchers identified victims in Myanmar, Mongolia, Pakistan, and Russia, including confirmed government entities.

Technologies: operating-system, antivirus

Products: windows, microsoft-defender, 360-total-security

Vendors: microsoft, sangfor, qihoo-360

You’re Back In The Room (Citrix NetScaler Pre-Auth RCE CVE-2026-8452(?)) — Must Read

watchTowr Labs details a pre-auth heap overflow in Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway SAML handling, likely CVE-2026-8452, that can be turned into remote code execution on vulnerable builds. The key takeaway is to patch NetScaler 14.1 to 14.1-72.61 or 13.1 to 13.1-63.18 or later, especially if SAML is enabled.

  • watchTowr Labs analyzed a heap overflow vulnerability patched in Citrix’s NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway security bulletin and believes it is likely CVE-2026-8452 based on the bulletin’s “Memory Overflow” description.
  • The vulnerability is reachable when a NetScaler appliance is configured to use SAML as either a Service Provider or an Identity Provider, and Citrix lists NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-72.61 and 13.1 before 13.1-63.18 as affected.
  • During SAML signature canonicalization, earlier NetScaler versions copied attacker-controlled data from the ds:SignedInfo element into a fixed-size global buffer without checking whether it fit.
  • The researchers found that an oversized PrefixList attribute in the SignedInfo structure could overflow NetScaler network buffer metadata and produce a write-what-where primitive.
  • The researchers demonstrated remote code execution by overwriting a NetScaler function pointer, jumping to shellcode on the executable heap, dropping a PHP webshell, and setting the SUID bit on /bin/sh.

Technologies: vpn, load-balancer, remote-access

Products: netscaler-adc, netscaler-gateway

Vendors: citrix

Data analyst sent to prison for stealing data, extorting employer — May Read

A former Brightly Software contractor was sentenced to two years in prison for stealing employee payroll and personal data, then trying to extort the company for $2.5 million in cryptocurrency. Brightly paid a small Bitcoin amount before the FBI traced the scheme to him and seized evidence from his home.

  • Former Brightly Software data analyst contractor Cameron Curry was sentenced to two years in prison for targeting the company in a $2.5 million extortion scheme.
  • Curry stole sensitive documents after gaining access to Brightly’s payroll information and corporate data, then used the alias “Loot” to email employees with threats to leak the data.
  • The extortion emails included screenshots of employees’ personally identifiable information, including names, dates of birth, home addresses, and compensation information.
  • Brightly paid $7,540 in Bitcoin to a cryptocurrency wallet controlled by Curry after receiving multiple extortion emails.
  • The FBI searched Curry’s residence on January 24 and seized electronic devices containing evidence that linked him to the extortion scheme.

Products: schooldude

Vendors: brightly-software, siemens

  • In observed intrusions, HoneyMyte used PlugX as the initial post-compromise implant before deploying CoolClient components through DLL sideloading with a legitimate Sangfor executable renamed as defender.exe.
  • The updated CoolClient execution chain includes libngs.dll as a first-stage loader, loadcert.ini as a second-stage component responsible for setup, injection, driver deployment, and persistence, and cert.ini as the final-stage implant for C2 communication and backdoor functionality.
  • Researchers identified victims in Myanmar, Mongolia, Pakistan, and Russia, including confirmed government entities.

Technologies: operating-system, antivirus

Products: windows, microsoft-defender, 360-total-security

Vendors: microsoft, sangfor, qihoo-360

You’re Back In The Room (Citrix NetScaler Pre-Auth RCE CVE-2026-8452(?)) — Must Read

watchTowr Labs detailed a pre-auth heap overflow in Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway SAML handling, likely CVE-2026-8452, that can be exploited for remote code execution. The issue affects NetScaler versions before 14.1-72.61 and 13.1-63.18, so impacted systems should be patched immediately.

  • watchTowr Labs analyzed a vulnerability patched in a recent NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway security bulletin and believes it is likely CVE-2026-8452, described by Citrix as a memory overflow issue.
  • The vulnerability is reachable when a NetScaler appliance is configured to use SAML as either a Service Provider or an Identity Provider.
  • Affected versions listed by Citrix are NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-72.61 and 13.1 before 13.1-63.18.
  • The bug occurs during SAML signature canonicalization, where attacker-controlled data from the ds:SignedInfo element can be copied into a fixed-size global buffer without checking whether it fits.
  • watchTowr Labs demonstrated that the heap overflow can be developed into remote code execution by gaining control of a write-what-where primitive, redirecting execution to shellcode, and dropping a PHP webshell.

Technologies: vpn, load-balancer, remote-access, operating-system, web-server

Products: netscaler-adc, netscaler-gateway, nsppe, freebsd, php

Vendors: citrix

Stealing the Artifact – JFrog Artifactory Vulnerability — Should Read

NetSPI found a chain of JFrog Artifactory vulnerabilities that let an unauthenticated attacker mint an anonymous JWT, bypass authorization, and retrieve restricted artifacts from affected repositories. JFrog has patched the issues in Artifactory 7.146.8 and several supported maintenance releases.

  • NetSPI discovered vulnerabilities in JFrog Artifactory that allowed an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and authorization to retrieve an arbitrary artifact from an Artifactory repository.
  • At the time of discovery, all versions of Artifactory OSS and Artifactory Enterprise were affected by the vulnerabilities.
  • CVE-2026-42018 allowed authentication bypass to the anonymous user and was remediated in Artifactory 7.146.8.
  • CVE-2026-69107 covered potential unauthorized artifact access and was remediated in Artifactory versions 7.146.8, 7.133.21, 7.125.14, 7.117.21, 7.111.14, and 7.104.16.
  • The attack chain combined four bugs: an anonymous JWT mint authentication bypass, missing authorization in stash results, path traversal in stash export, and URL path confusion.

Technologies: package-registry, ci-cd, iam, web-server, router, load-balancer

Products: artifactory, artifactory-oss, artifactory-enterprise, aws-iam, apache-tomcat, traefik, spring-security, jf-router

Vendors: jfrog, amazon-web-services, apache-software-foundation, traefik-labs, spring

Hackers arrested over €30M bank fraud exploiting service provider flaw — Should Read

Brazilian and European authorities arrested or charged suspects accused of exploiting a service-provider software flaw to trigger unauthorized direct debits from Commerzbank customer accounts, causing about €30 million in losses. Commerzbank said affected customers did not suffer financial losses.

  • Four cybercriminals were arrested in Brazil and three others were charged in Europe over allegations that they exploited a vulnerability at a service provider to withdraw funds from Commerzbank customers’ bank accounts.
  • The theft occurred over four days in November 2023 and caused losses of around €30 million, according to the investigation by Brazilian and German federal police agencies.
  • Commerzbank confirmed that its clients were impacted by unauthorized direct debits caused by technical issues at a service provider, but said customers suffered no financial loss.
  • German authorities said the attackers exploited a software vulnerability introduced by a faulty software update at the payment and transaction-processing system of a financial institution.
  • Investigators said the stolen funds were moved and concealed through pass-through accounts, companies, payment institutions, virtual-asset platforms, and payment cards issued without the beneficiaries’ consent.

Ransomware Threats in the Americas H1 2026: Dissecting the Regional Attack Patterns and Dominant Actors — Should Read

The Americas accounted for 57% of all ransomware incidents tracked globally in H1 2026, with the U.S. as the main target and Qilin the top regional actor. North America faces a crowded RaaS ecosystem, while South America is more concentrated around The Gentlemen, requiring different defensive priorities by region and sector.

  • Cyble Research and Intelligence Labs tracked 2,188 documented ransomware attacks in North and South America between January and June 2026, representing more than 57% of the 3,836 ransomware incidents tracked worldwide.
  • North America recorded 1,981 ransomware attacks in H1 2026, while South America recorded 207 attacks, with the article describing North America as a saturated market and South America as more concentrated around fewer operators.
  • Qilin was the most active ransomware group across the Americas with 410 documented incidents, while The Gentlemen was the most active group specifically in South America with 46 incidents.
  • The United States accounted for 1,721 ransomware attacks, representing 78.7% of Americas ransomware activity and nearly 45% of global ransomware volume tracked in the article.
  • The article identifies Professional Services, Manufacturing, Construction, Healthcare, BFSI, Agriculture and Livestock, and Government and Law Enforcement as sectors facing notable ransomware or related cyber threats across the Americas.

France investigates tax authority breach after hacker claims 600,000 victims — Should Read

France’s tax authority confirmed hackers accessed and extracted data from its systems after misusing someone’s identity, with a hacker claiming data on more than 600,000 people was stolen. Authorities are still verifying the scope and said affected individuals and businesses will be notified.

  • France’s Economy Ministry said an attacker gained unauthorized access to DGFiP systems in late June after stealing or misusing someone’s identity.
  • The intrusion allowed the attacker to view and extract data belonging to individuals and businesses, but officials are still determining exactly what information was accessed or stolen and how many people and businesses were affected.
  • A hacker using the alias ZeroBytes claimed to have obtained data on more than 600,000 people, including names, tax identification numbers, email addresses, family circumstances, and tax status details, though the claim has not been independently verified.
  • The DGFiP said affected people will be contacted individually with details about what information may have been exposed and what precautions they should take.
  • The agency said it would notify France’s data protection authority, file a criminal complaint, and provide further information as the investigation progresses.

Technologies: vpn

Data analyst sent to prison for stealing data, extorting employer — Should Read

Former Brightly Software contractor Cameron Curry was sentenced to two years in prison for stealing employee data and trying to extort the company for $2.5 million after his contract ended. Brightly paid $7,540 in Bitcoin before the FBI linked Curry to the scheme through seized devices.

  • Former Brightly Software data analyst contractor Cameron Curry was sentenced to two years in prison for targeting his employer in a $2.5 million extortion scheme.
  • Court documents said Curry stole sensitive documents after gaining access to Brightly’s payroll information and corporate data when he learned his six-month contract would not be extended.
  • Between December 11, 2023, and January 24, 2024, Curry used the alias “Loot” and the email address lootsoftware@outlook.com to threaten Brightly employees with leaking stolen information unless the company paid a $2.5 million cryptocurrency ransom.
  • Curry attached screenshots of employees’ personally identifiable information, including names, dates of birth, home addresses, and compensation information, and threatened to report Brightly to the SEC for failing to disclose the breach.
  • Brightly paid $7,540 in Bitcoin before the FBI searched Curry’s residence on January 24 and seized electronic devices containing evidence linking him to the extortion scheme.

Products: schooldude

Vendors: brightly-software, siemens

Apple sent a new batch of high-confidence Threat Notifications warning some iPhone users they were individually targeted by mercenary spyware. Recipients should verify the alert through account.apple.com, avoid clicking links in messages, enable Lockdown Mode, and seek expert help.

  • Users can verify a genuine Apple Threat Notification by signing in directly to account.apple.com, where the alert will appear at the top of the page if Apple sent one.

Products: apple-threat-notifications, iphone, pegasus, lockdown-mode, apple-account, imessage

Vendors: apple, nso-group

The Tracking Parameter That Named the Wrong Company — May Read

A Microsoft Teams-themed phishing email reused a multi-layer redirect kit, exposing a stale tracking parameter tied to an unrelated organization and showing that the attacker’s most durable fingerprint was the template structure rather than the domains used. The case highlights why defenders should fully decode redirect chains and hunt for reused kit artifacts like hidden CSS, encoding patterns, and leftover tracking identifiers.

  • A director-level mailbox at a mid-size forensic engineering and investigative consulting firm received a fabricated Microsoft Teams audio-message notification with a single “Listen to Message” button.
  • Decoding the button’s destination revealed four nested layers ending at a payment-themed path on the apex domain of a Brazilian law firm that has held the domain registration since 2004.
  • A leftover recipient-tracking parameter in the final redirect named an employee address at an unrelated organization, which the article says indicates reused phishing-kit plumbing rather than evidence that the named organization was breached or involved.
  • The lure used hidden CSS, short hex-like fragments, and a zero-width space to split brand words such as Microsoft, Teams, and audio message while keeping them readable to humans.
  • SPF and composite authentication passed, DKIM was absent, DMARC returned a best-guess pass, and the article says the behavioral signals drove the phishing classification.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis, adaptive-ai, microsoft-teams

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft

How Anthropic plans to watermark Claude's AI-generated text — May Read

Anthropic will add invisible text watermarking to Claude outputs worldwide to comply with the EU AI Act, using statistical patterns in token choices rather than hidden characters. The watermark can be checked through a planned detection API, but it works best on longer, more creative text and may be weaker for code, factual answers, or heavily rewritten content.

  • Anthropic plans to add invisible watermarking to future Claude-generated text worldwide as part of its compliance with the EU AI Act and the EU Code of Practice.
  • Anthropic says Claude’s text watermark does not add visible markers, hidden characters, extra tokens, added cost, or a practical impact on creativity, readability, content quality, or generation speed.
  • The watermarking approach is based on Google DeepMind’s SynthID-Text and works by using a secret key to influence some of Claude’s random word choices during generation, creating a statistical pattern detectable by someone with the key.
  • Anthropic says watermarking is weaker or not applied when an exact output is required, such as factual answers or code, and detection is less reliable for short text or light proofreading of human-written text.
  • Anthropic plans to offer a watermark detection API that can estimate whether Claude was likely involved in writing text, while generated PNG, JPG, and SVG files will use cryptographically signed C2PA provenance metadata instead of text-style watermarking.

Products: claude, synthid-text

Vendors: anthropic, google-deepmind

The Modern Attack Chain: Rethinking Google Workspace Security in the Age of AI — Optional

The article argues that Google Workspace security can no longer focus only on email, because attackers and AI agents can use OAuth access to reach Gmail and Drive, steal sensitive data, and pivot across apps. Organizations need visibility and controls across OAuth grants, email, Drive, and account behavior to limit both malicious and unintended access.

  • The article argues that the Vercel and Composio breaches followed the same pattern in which email was not the entry point into the workspace.
  • The described evolving attack chain begins with a stolen OAuth token, which can provide persistent access to Gmail and Drive and may survive password resets.
  • The article says attackers can use access to Gmail and Drive to read sensitive data, take over email accounts, and move laterally through password resets, magic links, or credentials stored in Drive.
  • The article warns that authorized AI agents connected to Google Workspace can read email and Drive data through legitimate OAuth grants and may follow a similar path if they behave unexpectedly or have overly broad access.
  • The article states that defenses should cover email, OAuth behavior, Drive data, and account activity together rather than focusing only on the inbox.

Technologies: email-security, dlp, casb, iam, cloud-platform

Products: google-workspace, gmail, google-drive, material-email-security, material-file-security

Vendors: material-security, google

Over-Tooled, Under-Coordinated: The Real Cost of Tool Sprawl — Optional

Security teams are struggling less from lack of data than from fragmented tool stacks that force analysts to manually correlate evidence across many consoles, slowing investigations and weakening confidence. The key fix is better coordination of classification, policy, and evidence across tools and data flows, not simply buying more products or consolidating everything into one tool.

  • 58% of organizations now run 11 or more separate data security tools, while only 7% describe their stack as fully unified.
  • 45% of security teams query six or more separate systems per investigation, and 16% query more than 10.
  • Only 9% of organizations can fully investigate nearly all sensitive-data alerts, while 56% investigate half or fewer.
  • Visibility is weakest in AI tools at 10%, and only 7% of organizations can track sensitive data moving between applications in real time.
  • Only 12% of organizations can quickly produce a comprehensive, auditable chain of custody, and 46% require significant manual effort across systems or struggle to produce sufficient evidence.

Vendors: cybersecurity-insiders, netskope

FileRun: When Your File Manager Runs Your Files — Optional

The article analyzes a FileRun security flaw that can let attackers turn the web-based file manager into a path for running malicious files on the server. The key takeaway is that exposed FileRun instances should be patched and locked down to prevent remote code execution.

  • The article is titled "FileRun: When Your File Manager Runs Your Files."
  • The article identifies FileRun as the subject.
  • The title frames the article around a file manager that runs files.

Products: filerun

Vendors: filerun

  • It says enterprise-grade DAST should support authenticated testing, endpoint and API discovery, API protocol coverage, exploit validation, governance, compliance reporting, complementary pentesting, and predictable pricing.
  • The article argues that DAST is useful because it tests running applications for weaknesses such as SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and authentication bypasses, but it does not catch business-logic flaws like broken authorization or skippable workflow steps.
  • Aikido Security is presented as combining authenticated DAST, live-traffic API discovery, attack surface monitoring, exploit validation, RBAC, SSO, policy enforcement, and autonomous AI pentesting in one platform.
  • The article states that other tools such as Invicti, Burp Suite DAST, Rapid7 InsightAppSec, Checkmarx DAST, HCL AppScan, and Qualys WAS are better suited to specific needs such as standard web apps, in-house security teams, regulated environments, or existing platform commitments.

  • The article compares Aikido Security, Sonatype, Snyk, Endor Labs, Checkmarx, Black Duck, and Veracode on real-time intelligence, governance and policy enforcement, compliance coverage, and triage at enterprise scale.

  • The article states that compliance frameworks such as CRA and NIS2 require supply chain security, including portfolio-wide SBOM management, license risk tracking, and visibility into which applications are affected by new threats.

item.title: Akira, Jewelbug, JWR Phishing, and Ukraine Call Center Takedowns
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Aug 18:00 → 13 Aug 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers breach govt webmail while running parallel crypto fraud — Should Read

The China-linked Jewelbug group compromised shared government webmail infrastructure in the Middle East to steal cookies, credentials, and emails while also running a large-scale crypto fraud operation from the same control panel. Symantec says the group’s tooling and infrastructure show parallel espionage and financially motivated activity, including fake crypto exchange pages, malicious browser extensions, and custom implants.

  • The China-based Jewelbug hacker group compromised webmail accounts belonging to 15 government tenants in a campaign targeting a country in the Middle East.
  • Symantec found that Jewelbug inserted a malicious script into a shared webmail template, allowing it to run on login pages and mailbox views across the affected tenants.
  • The malicious script connected to the attackers’ command-and-control server, stole webmail cookies, retrieved users’ email addresses, and delivered a fake Adobe Flash update prompt to selected government targets.
  • Symantec said Jewelbug’s victim database contained more than one million implant check-in rows, more than 580,000 stolen browser cookies, several thousand captured credentials, and more than 2,300 exfiltrated email bodies.
  • Symantec reported that Jewelbug also ran an industrial-scale cryptocurrency fraud operation using AI-generated articles, fake crypto exchange sites, click-fraud bots, and hundreds of lookalike domains impersonating OKX and Binance.

Technologies: remote-access, browser, router

Products: antino, xg-web, pdf-viewer, clientking, adobe-flash, google-docs, google-chrome, mozilla-firefox, asus-routers, okx, binance

Vendors: adobe, google, mozilla, asus, okx, binance

Akira hackers disable EDR with Safe Mode, steal data but fail to encrypt — Should Read

An Akira ransomware affiliate used a SonicWall VPN account without MFA to breach a network, rebooted a host into Safe Mode with Networking to disable Huntress EDR and Microsoft Defender protections, and stole data. The ransomware encryption attempt failed due to system errors, but the attackers still completed credential and data theft in under five hours.

  • An Akira ransomware affiliate gained initial access through an exposed SonicWall VPN device that did not have multi-factor authentication enabled.
  • After logging in, the attacker used RDP to reach the domain controller, enumerated Active Directory users and computers, and moved to an application server.
  • The attacker used WinRAR to archive mapped file shares and s5cmd to upload stolen data to an attacker-controlled S3 bucket before installing AnyDesk for remote access.
  • The attacker rebooted the compromised host into Safe Mode with Networking, disabled the Huntress agent and Microsoft Defender real-time protection, and added AnyDesk to the Windows Safe Mode registry to preserve access.
  • The Akira ransomware payload failed to execute in Safe Mode because of low virtual memory and related errors, but the attacker still stole credentials and files in less than five hours from initial access.

Technologies: edr, antivirus, operating-system, vpn, remote-access, object-storage

Products: huntress-agent, microsoft-defender, windows, active-directory, sonicwall-vpn, anydesk, winrar, s5cmd, amazon-s3

Vendors: huntress, microsoft, sonicwall, anydesk, rarlab, amazon-web-services

Ukraine shuts down 94 fraudulent call centers, seize millions in cash — Should Read

Ukrainian authorities shut down 94 fraudulent call centers that ran bank impersonation, fake investment, and recovery scams targeting victims in Ukraine and the EU. Police seized thousands of devices, SIM cards, cash, crypto wallet access tools, vehicles, and gold, and identified 26 suspects who could face up to 12 years in prison.

  • Ukrainian authorities shut down 94 fraudulent call centers after 411 searches conducted with involvement from the National Police, Ukraine's Security Service, the Prosecutor General’s Office, and German police.
  • The call centers ran schemes in which operators posed as bankers, brokers, and law enforcement officers to lure victims into fake investment platforms or gain access to their bank accounts.
  • Police said some call centers targeted people in foreign countries, particularly in the European Union, and tricked them into investing on fake brokerage platforms and installing remote-access software.
  • During the raids, police seized 1,794 fully equipped workstations, 3,336 pieces of computer equipment, 1,346 phones, 5,200 SIM cards, 90 bank cards, access tools for 20 cryptocurrency wallets, 22 vehicles, cash, and gold.
  • Twenty-six individuals have been formally notified that they are suspects, and the offenses under investigation carry penalties of up to 12 years in prison and confiscation of property.

Curiouser and Curiouser — Optional

Cisco Talos highlights JWR, a real-time phishing framework used in SMS scams that lets attackers interact with victims live to steal payment data, identity documents, device fingerprints, and MFA codes. Organizations should prioritize smishing awareness, monitor unusual logins, and adopt phishing-resistant MFA such as FIDO2 keys.

  • Cisco Talos recently discovered “JWR,” a previously undocumented, real-time phishing framework and likely variant of “The Outsider” phishing-as-a-service platform.
  • JWR uses an open WebSocket connection that allows attackers to monitor keystrokes live and dynamically steer victims through fake checkout and login flows.
  • JWR is currently deployed via SMS lures impersonating regional toll and postal authorities to steal payment data, 2FA codes, identity documents, and device fingerprints.
  • The article says JWR can help attackers bypass multi-factor authentication by prompting victims for 2FA codes exactly when needed.
  • The article recommends user education around SMS-based phishing, monitoring for unusual authentication attempts, and implementing phishing-resistant MFA methods like FIDO2 hardware keys where possible.

Technologies: mfa

Products: jwr, the-outsider, microsoft-sharepoint, signal, shopify

Vendors: cisco, microsoft, signal-foundation, shopify
